title: Gamliel Zuga
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman writes that he is mentioned only in the Jerusalem Talmud, and he lived in the third-to-fourth generation.

He also merited to see Rabbi Yochanan: see Challah ch. 4 halakhah 3, where he asked Rabbi Yochanan, and Orlah beginning of ch. 2, where Rabbi Yochanan asked him whether they separate lachah [supplied לחה; compare challah, חלה] from demai produce, and he told him no. (And see the entry on R’ Berechiah.)

Hyman also says he received teaching from Resh Lakish: see Avodah Zarah ch. 3 halakhah 11, where he once went with Resh Lakish, and when they reached an object of idolatry he asked him whether it is permitted to pass before it; and Sukkah ch. 3 halakhah 1, where he made a sukkah in the public domain and Resh Lakish passed by and said, 'Who permitted you?'

He also asked Rabbi Mana [extra supplied ר׳ remains unresolved] (see the Jerusalem Talmud end of Beitzah; Moed Katan ch. 3 halakhah 5, 12b). He also asked Rabbi Yasa (Jerusalem Talmud end of Terumot; whom Hyman identifies as Rabbi Assi, citing Shabbat beginning of ch. 2), and he asked Rabbi Ba bar Kahana (Demai end of ch. 2), and Hyman says that this is how one must read in Nedarim ch. 8 halakhah 4. And in Berakhot ch. 6 halakhah 4, Gamliel Zuga went up to those of the house of Rabbi Yannai (whose academy was in the city of Akhbara); and in Peah ch. 8 halakhah 3, those of the house of Ami [supplied בית אמי; named edition: Assi] cooked a vegetable and forgot to separate its required tithes; Gamliel Zuga went up and separated them. We also find that he asked Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Bun, 'Which is the clearest of all [these prooftexts]?' He said to him, 'And you shall be clean,' etc. (Shekalim ch. 3, end of halakhah 2).

We find that he had a brother named Hillel (Moed Katan ch. 3 halakhah 5, 12b: when his sister died, Hillel his brother went up with him). The scholar designated הה״ח ר״ז יעבץ, in vol. 7 p. 187, says that he is R’ Gamliel the fifth, son of R’ Yehudah Nesiah the Second, and says there that he asked his father (Kilayim end of ch. 2). Hyman replies: With all due respect, all his words are mistaken: there it says that Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Vales asked his father, and he was never a nasi.

notes.text: 'Pe'a went' (פ"א הלך) appears garbled in the Hebrew; translated literally and left uncertain. 'כ' before references appears to be a printed 'see' marker and is rendered 'see'. Reference markers like 'ב' rendered 'in'.

The abbreviation 'הה"ח ר"ז יעבץ' is unclear; rendered tentatively as the author R. Z. Yavetz, with 'Hatzofeh/Ha-Hakham' expansion uncertain. 'ר' כירושלמי' also unclear. Hebrew retained where uncertain.
The Hebrew of 'ר"ז יעבץ' likely refers to Ze'ev Yavetz, but the exact expansion is not supplied.

In the named Guggenheimer Peah 8:3 paragraph, fixing the cooked vegetables concerns giving the required heave/tithes, not repairing or seasoning them. Ami in the supplied text remains distinct from Assi in that edition. The complete Shekalim 3:2 paragraph cites Torah, Prophets and Writings proofs before the question “Which is clearest?”; the bracketed prooftexts referent clarifies the question without adding a new speaker or changing Hyman’s quote.
The question concerns their practice (whether they separate), not a newly inserted permission question. Supplied לחה and Hyman’s abbreviated NO remain distinct from the longer named חלה discussion.

This remains Hyman’s account. His chronological, familial, teacher and identity judgments and proposed corrections are attributed to him. Historical draft notes n1–n3 are retained: the former “Pe’a” reading is superseded by “once”; the Hatzofeh/Ha-Hakham expansion is unsupported and is not adopted; the possible given-name expansion of R.Z. Yavetz remains unconfirmed. Source-specific R’ titles are retained where their expansion has not been established.

The consulted Nedarim 8:4 reads Rabbi Ba bar Zavda, while Demai 2:1 reads Rabbi Ba bar Kahana; Hyman’s proposed correction and his supplied Demai locator are preserved. Terumot 11:5 reads Rabbi Yasa, while Shabbat 2:1 reads Rabbi Issi; Hyman’s Assi identification remains his claim. The complete consulted Kilayim 2:8 paragraph reports both Rabbi Gamliel Beribbi asking his father and Rabbi Hillel bar Wales asking his father. This is disclosed alongside Hyman’s criticism without identifying Gamliel Zuga with a patriarch or adding an alternative identity.

Hyman's printed notice (vol. I, p. 305) reads חלה, ‘challah,’ and עם, ‘with,’ where the supplied Hebrew has לחה and אם. In the consulted Orlah 2:1, Gamliel answers the question about local practice with a statement by Samuel, brother of Rav Berechiah, and Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun then gives a further ruling. Hyman summarizes the answer as ‘no’; Guggenheimer's note reads it as affirmative. The print also reads א׳ after Rabbi Mana, where the supplied text has ר׳. The consulted Beitzah and Moed Katan passages name Rabbi Mana without numbering him. Hyman's printed ‘house of Ami’ differs from the ‘house of Assi’ in the consulted Peah 8:3.

In the consulted 1963 edition of Ze'ev Yavetz's Toledot Yisrael (vol. 7, ‘Caesarea’), Yavetz identifies Gamliel Zuga with the fifth patriarch and says he succeeded his father, Yehudah Nesiah II. His note 153 cites Kilayim for asking his father. The consulted Kilayim passage has two separate episodes, one in which Rabbi Gamliel Beribbi asks his father and another in which Rabbi Hillel bar Wales asks his father. The latter is the person Hyman names in his objection. These passages document the competing readings; Gamliel Beribbi's identification with Gamliel Zuga remains Yavetz's conclusion. The original p. 187 citation has not been collated.
